extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, regulated entities, legal practitioners, advocates, and agency staff searching Federal Register documents concerning Section 1557 and related rulemaking/notice-and-comment activity
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register search-results/listing page that aggregates titles, abstracts, and excerpts of documents that mention or implement Section 1557 of the Affordable Care Act (nondiscrimination in health programs). The page is intended to help users find rulemakings, notices, proposed/final rules, and related documents for review and comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 1557 nondiscrimination prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1557 prohibits discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability in certain health programs and activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used repeatedly as the substantive legal baseline across multiple documents (proposed rules, final rules, notices). This is the central statutory standard agencies reference when assessing whether policies/programs discriminate in health programs and activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 1557(c) rulemaking authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1557(c) of the ACA authorizes the Secretary of the Department to promulgate regulations to implement the nondiscrimination requirements of section 1557.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited as the statutory authority for HHS and CMS to issue regulations and guidance implementing Section 1557; grounds agencies' regulatory actions and interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability: Medicare Part B as Federal financial assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Medicare Part B constitutes Federal financial assistance for purposes of civil rights enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department indicates it is revising its interpretation on this point; the determination affects whether entities/activities tied to Medicare Part B fall within Section 1557 enforcement scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of nondiscrimination provisions across programs and actors
rubrics_metrics.description: Revisions to nondiscrimination provisions to prohibit discrimination (including on the basis of sexual orientation and gender identity) in regulations issued by CMS governing Medicaid and CHIP; Programs of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly (PACE); health insurance issuers and their officials, employees, agents, and representatives; States and the Exchanges carrying out Exchange requirements; agents, brokers, or web-brokers that assist with or facilitate enrollment of qualified individuals, qualified employers, or qualified employees; issuers providing essential health benefits (EHB); and qualified health plan issuers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents on the page assert or propose expanding or clarifying the set of programs, plans, and actors to which Section 1557's nondiscrimination obligations apply, including explicit mention of sexual orientation and gender identity in some rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) ICR public comment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In compliance with the requirement of the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, agencies submit Information Collection Requests (ICRs) to OMB for review and approval and publish notices inviting public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple documents reference 30-day and 60-day public comment requests, summaries of proposed collections (nature of information and expected burden), and that OMB will accept public comments during its review — procedural requirements for agency information collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parenthetical/definition of 'sex' in Section 1557/Title IX materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify the parenthetical definitions of sex for Title IX and Section 1557 to hew closely to the statutory text; such revision conforms to E.O. 14168 and the court order in Texas v. Becerra staying nationwide the Section 1557 Final Rule definition of sex discrimination as including 'sex characteristics, including intersex traits'; 'pregnancy or related conditions'; 'sexual orientation'; 'gender identity'; and 'sex stereotypes'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The excerpts show agencies revising or proposing to revise definitional language about 'sex' in response to Executive Orders and court decisions; the scope of protected 'sex' characteristics is therefore both a substantive criterion and subject to litigation/stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescission of agency guidance (retail pharmacies example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rescission of 'Guidance to Nation's Retail Pharmacies: Obligations under Federal Civil Rights Laws to Ensure Nondiscriminatory Access to Health Care at Pharmacies' and related guidance (effective upon publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency rescission is used to remove prior informal guidance that reminded pharmacies they must comply with civil rights laws such as Section 1557 and Section 504; rescission reduces 'burdens on regulated parties' per the excerpt and reflects a change in enforcement/interpretation emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurances required by federal civil rights laws in agency submissions/ICRs
rubrics_metrics.description: Such an assurance is required by the federal civil rights laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some ICRs and forms must include assurances (presumably of nondiscrimination compliance) because federal civil rights statutes require them; agencies reference this as a condition in information collection or program administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction of programmatic rules with Section 1557 (example: Medicaid/CHIP funding restrictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: When issuing programmatic rules (e.g., prohibiting Federal Medicaid/CHIP funding for specified procedures), agencies state whether such rules are 'a form of sex discrimination in violation of section 1557' and explain intersections with nondiscrimination law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulemaking texts include analyses stating whether proposed program restrictions implicate Section 1557; agencies use Section 1557 to assess legal risk/consistency when changing coverage/payment rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 1557's relationship to other civil-rights statutes and case law
rubrics_metrics.description: References and cross-citation of Section 1557 to Title IX, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, the ADA, Title VII, Equal Protection Clause, and case law (e.g., Texas v. Becerra; Grimm; Boyden; Prescott; Tovar; Doe v. Snyder).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents commonly discuss Section 1557 in the context of other civil-rights authorities and judicial interpretations; agencies rely on case law and cross-statutory analogies to interpret scope, defenses, and enforcement mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of Long COVID as potential disability under ADA/Section 504/Section 1557
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on 'Long COVID' as a disability under the ADA, section 504, and section 1557.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced guidance (HHS/DOJ) treats Long COVID as potentially qualifying as a disability, which informs agencies' nondiscrimination analyses and obligations toward individuals with Long COVID in health programs and activities.
